answer: Based on the provided evidence, neutropenia is the most common adverse reaction with IBRANCE (80% in PALOMA-2, 83% in PALOMA-3, any grade) [4][5]. In PALOMA-2/-3, median time to first any-grade neutropenia was 15 days, with median duration of Grade ≥3 neutropenia of 7 days, and it was generally reversible, non-cumulative, and manageable without growth factor support [2][3]. However, the evidence set does not specify exact CBC monitoring intervals or dose-adjustment thresholds recommended in the label. For complete monitoring guidance (e.g., baseline and periodic CBC schedule), please consult the full Prescribing Information or escalate to Medical Information.
